title: His son Bobby Leeman, pianist for Dionne Warwick
summary: Son Bobby, born in 1940, studied at the New England Conservatory, overcame problems, accompanied Dionne Warwick and died suddenly of pneumonia.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: We discussed that -- we've been
digressing a bit -- did we discuss whether you had any brothers or sisters?
A half-sister.
Yeah, we mentioned you had a half sister. So now we're mentioning your first wife. I'm just trying to get some family connections here. And your first wife, you had some children by her?
My Bobby.
What was his name?
Bobby Leeman, Robert Leeman. He was a great pianist.
Great pianist.
And he died three years ago.
Yes, I remember that.

He was born March 1st, 1940, and he became one of -- when my first wife and I separated, he lived in Boston with her, and her second husband -- and then he was going for private instruction at the Conservatory of Music when he was 14 or 15.
Which one?
Bobby. Played piano.
Do you remember what conservatory?
Yeah, the New England Conservatory.
Marvelous.
And he did very well.
I know he did very well. I happen to
know some of the things he did.
And he had problems during the era when all young musicians had problems -- and he got himself straightened out. He straightened out beautifully, and he was ... (CUT)
... about your son, Bobby -- you said he got straightened out, he had problems but he got straightened out, so continue from that.
Well, he was quite a talent, in other peoples' minds, too. He did something that a lot of great pianists can't do -- is accompany singers. That's an art in itself, as you know.
Uh huh.

And he eventually ended up with Dionne Warwick three years ago, or 4 years ago, and he was doing some writing for her, doing some charts, and also playing piano for her. He was the leader with a small group that she would take out, and he played -- oh, I don't know the conductor's name, I saw him in a movie, they made at Wolf Trap; and he had a wonderful future, because Dionne three years ago had some movies coming out and some great things coming, and Bobby had the flu. I was at sea at the time, I was doing the thing with Major Holley, and so forth, and Bob had such a future, and got pneumonia overnight, and his wife was rushing him to the Southern California clinic, and he died in the car.
That was a great tragedy, we all read about it, and ...
Yeah, pneumonia, and they didn't realize it.
Oh, it was a great tragedy, and we all felt so sadly about it because you were away.
Especially him coming into his own at the time, but of course, he lived a full life ...
